mainTopic: Danger and the protection of שלוחי מצוה in בדיקת חמץ, and which rows of barrels must be checked in a wine cellar
overview: This amud opens by finishing the question of why a person checking holes for חמץ needs to fear danger, when שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקין. The first answer is that he may go back to look for his lost needle after the מצוה is finished. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the danger differently. Following the תנא פלימו, he says it comes from a non-Jewish neighbor, who might suspect כשפים when he sees someone searching with a candle at night. The גמרא then teaches that the protection of a מצוה does not cover places where danger is common, and proves this from שמואל's fear of שאול. Next, רב is asked whether students may travel in the dark to learn. רבי אלעזר rules that שלוחי מצוה are protected both going and returning, based on איסי בן יהודה's ברייתא about עלייה לרגל. Two short sayings explain that the fruits of גינוסר and the hot springs of טבריא are not in ירושלים, so that pilgrims go up only for the מצוה. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה about checking 'two rows' of barrels in a wine cellar. It explains the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל, and rules like שמואל: check the top front row and the top row just behind it.

steps.title: Even with a personal motive, he is still fully righteous
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: a person who does a מצוה while also having a personal goal is still a צדיק גמור, so he should still be protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: This person is a completely righteous person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge that began on the previous amud. If giving צדקה "so that my son will live" still makes someone a צדיק גמור, then someone checking for חמץ who also looks for his needle is still doing a full מצוה and should be protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said he loses protection because he is also looking for his own needle. This line attacks that answer. A personal motive mixed into a מצוה does not cancel the מצוה, so the protection of שלוחי מצוה should still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is (introduces a legal status)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the punchline of a ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section, about someone who gives a סלע to צדקה so his son will live. It is being used here as a challenge.

phrases.english: This one is a completely righteous person!
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא about giving צדקה with a personal motive, used here as a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge from the previous section of the דף against the 'lost needle' explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that looking for a lost needle removes the protection of שלוחי מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A personal motive does not cancel a מצוה, so the person should still count as a שליח מצוה and be protected.

steps.title: He may search for the needle after the checking is done
steps.stepSummary: The danger exists because he may go back to look for the needle after he has already finished the בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps after he has finished checking, he will come back to look for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The worry is about a later moment, after the מצוה of checking is already over, when he goes back just for his needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees that a mixed motive does not cancel a מצוה. It moves the danger to a time when no מצוה is happening at all. At that point he is no longer a שליח מצוה, so he has no protection.

phrases.english: Perhaps after he has checked
phrases.notes: After the בדיקת חמץ is completed.

phrases.english: he will come to look for it (the needle)
phrases.notes: Now he is acting only for himself, not for a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the timing of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The danger happens while he is checking, so a mixed motive would matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The danger happens after the checking is finished, when no מצוה protects him.

steps.title: A different explanation: the danger comes from גוים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the danger in the תוספתא is from גוים, and the ruling follows the תנא פלימו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is because of the danger from the גוים, and it follows the view of פלימו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a completely new explanation of what 'danger' the תוספתא means. It is a danger from non-Jewish neighbors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of talking about a needle or other physical dangers, he says the danger comes from people, the גוים. He also identifies whose opinion this is: the תנא פלימו. The next step shows the source for this.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is because of the danger of the gentiles,
and it (the תוספתא) follows Pelimu.
phrases.notes: Not everyone agrees; this is פלימו's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation of the 'danger', in place of the needle approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger in the תוספתא is from גוים, following פלימו.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a hole between a Jew and a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says to check as far as your hand reaches and do ביטול on the rest. פלימו says not to check that hole at all because of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A hole between a Jew and a non-Jew — one checks as far as his hand reaches, and nullifies the rest in his heart. פלימו says: he does not check it at all, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to show where פלימו's opinion comes from. It concerns a hole in a shared wall between a Jew's house and a non-Jew's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת. The first opinion says to check partway and rely on ביטול for the rest. פלימו says to skip the checking entirely 'because of the danger', which matches the תוספתא's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifies it in his heart (ביטול חמץ)

phrases.english: As it was taught: A hole between a Jew and a gentile —
he checks as far as his hand reaches,
and the rest he nullifies in his heart.
Pelimu said:
He does not check it at all
phrases.notes: Not even the part his hand can reach.

phrases.english: because of the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the תוספתא follows פלימו.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'danger' ruling is פלימו's view, about a hole bordering a non-Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of חור שבין יהודי לארמאי

steps.title: What danger? If it is suspicion of כשפים, how did he ever use the hole?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what danger is meant. If the non-Jew suspects כשפים, then the Jew could never have used the hole in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: What danger? If we say it is the danger of being suspected of witchcraft — then when he used the hole, how did he use it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of danger פלימו means. It then challenges the obvious guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking for חמץ is only needed in places where חמץ is normally brought. If the non-Jew would suspect the Jew of witchcraft whenever he touches the hole, the Jew could never have used it. In that case it would never need checking anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Danger of being suspected of witchcraft

phrases.english: What danger?
If we say the danger of witchcraft,
phrases.notes: The non-Jew would think the Jew is casting spells on him.

phrases.english: when he used it, how did he use it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי סַכָּנָה, אִי נֵימָא סַכָּנַת כְּשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of 'danger' in פלימו's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining פלימו's danger as suspicion of כשפים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If touching the hole causes suspicion, he could never have used it, so there would be no need to check it.

steps.title: Daytime use is fine; nighttime checking by candle raises suspicion
steps.stepSummary: He used the hole by day with no suspicion. Checking happens at night with a candle, which looks like witchcraft.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, when he used it, it was day and light, and the non-Jew did not think about it. Here it is night and with a candle, and he does think about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is the time and the way it is done. Normal use in the daytime looks innocent. Poking around with a candle at night looks like witchcraft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suspicion of כשפים is accepted, and the challenge is resolved by splitting the two situations. בדיקת חמץ is done at night by candlelight, which is exactly what makes it look suspicious.

phrases.english: There, when he used it —
it was day and light,
and he (the gentile) does not suspect anything.
Here — it is night and with a lamp,
and he does suspect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between two situations (day use versus night checking)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any contact with the hole would raise suspicion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only nighttime searching by candle raises suspicion of כשפים.

steps.title: But שלוחי מצוה are protected from harm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: רבי אלעזר said that people doing a מצוה are not harmed, so why worry about danger?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: People on a mission for a מצוה are not harmed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the basic problem. A person checking for חמץ is doing a מצוה, so he should be protected from the non-Jew too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge goes against רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation. The needle answer worked because the danger came after the מצוה. Here the danger happens during the checking itself, so the protection should apply.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)
People on a mission to do a מצוה

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Those on a mission for a מצוה are not harmed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole idea of danger during the checking, as now explained by רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one skips checking because of danger from גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח מצוה is protected, and the checking itself is a מצוה, so there should be no danger.

steps.title: Where harm is common, it is different
steps.stepSummary: The protection of שלוחי מצוה does not cover situations where danger is common and expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where harm is common, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's rule has a limit. It does not apply where danger is common and likely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule still stands, but it does not cover every case. When danger is common, a person may not rely on a miracle. An angry neighbor who suspects witchcraft is a common danger.

phrases.english: Where harm is common, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שליח מצוה is protected from every danger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The protection does not cover dangers that are common.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, שכיח היזיקא, is used throughout ש״ס and in הלכה. Even while doing a מצוה, one must avoid common dangers.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל, who feared שאול
steps.stepSummary: Even when ה׳ Himself sent שמואל to anoint דוד, שמואל feared שאול, and ה׳ gave him a cover story. This shows that common danger is a real concern even during a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And שמואל said: How can I go? שאול will hear and kill me. And ה׳ said: Take a calf in your hand..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer from a פסוק. שמואל was on a mission from ה׳, yet he worried about a common danger. ה׳ agreed and gave him a way to be careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being a שליח מצוה protected against every danger, שמואל would have had nothing to fear. ה׳ did not tell him he would be safe. Instead He gave him a cover story, a calf for a קרבן. This shows that common dangers must still be avoided.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the 'danger' in checking holes. The first is the needle that he looks for after the מצוה is done. The second, from רב נחמן בר יצחק following פלימו, is a non-Jewish neighbor who suspects witchcraft when he sees a candle at night. The rule שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקין does not apply where danger is common, as we see from שמואל.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Samuel said: How can I go?
Saul will hear and kill me;
And God said: A calf of the herd
take in your hand, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל Ⅰ 16:2. The calf is a cover story: he will say he came to bring a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the answer of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That common danger is a real concern even for a שליח מצוה

steps.title: Students ask רב about traveling in the dark to learn
steps.stepSummary: רב's students live out in the fields. They ask whether they may come to the בית מדרש before dawn and after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב: The students of רב's school who live out in the fields, may they come early (before dawn) and late (after dark) to רב's school?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life question that was asked of רב. Students who live far away want to know if they may travel in the dark to learn תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling in the dark through open fields was dangerous because of robbers and wild animals. The question is whether going to learn תורה, which is a מצוה, protects them enough to take this risk.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him (a question was raised before him)
Fields or open country outside the town
Early (before dawn) and in the dark (after nightfall)

phrases.english: They asked Rav:
These students of Rav's school
who live in the fields,
what is the law about coming early and in the dark
to Rav's school?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical case that tests how far the protection of שלוחי מצוה reaches, the topic from steps 7-9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May students travel in dangerous darkness to reach the בית מדרש, relying on the protection of the מצוה?

steps.title: רב: let them come, I take responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רב tells them to come and says the responsibility is on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Let them come, and it is on me and on my neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the students may travel to learn even in the dark. He personally takes responsibility for their safety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is confident that the מצוה protects them on the way to learning. The words 'on my neck' show how sure he is.

keyTerms.meaning: On me and on my neck, meaning 'I take full responsibility'

phrases.english: He said to them: Let them come,
it is upon me and upon my neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: נֵיתוֹ עֲלַי וְעַל צַוָּארִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 for the trip there.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Going to learn is protected, so they may come, and רב takes responsibility.

steps.title: What about going back home?
steps.stepSummary: The students follow up: what about the trip home?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about going (back home)?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a follow-up question. They want to know if the same protection applies on the way home after learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the way home the person has already finished the מצוה. So it is unclear whether he still counts as a שליח מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To go (here: to go back home)

phrases.english: What about going back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from going to returning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the protection of the מצוה also cover the return trip?

steps.title: רב: I do not know
steps.stepSummary: רב says he does not know whether the return trip is protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב admits he is unsure whether the protection continues on the trip home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was ready to take full responsibility for the trip there, but he will not say the same for the trip back. The next step brings רבי אלעזר, who answers this question.

phrases.english: He said to them: I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by leaving the return trip unresolved.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב is uncertain about the return trip.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: protected both going and returning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that שלוחי מצוה are not harmed, either going or returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי אלעזר said: People sent on a מצוה are not harmed, not on their way there and not on their way back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clear rule from רבי אלעזר. It answers the question רב left open: the protection covers the return trip too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was unsure about returning, but רבי אלעזר states outright that returning is also protected. This is a fuller version of the rule quoted in step 7, which mentioned only the basic protection.

keyTerms.meaning: People on the way to do a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב and רבי אלעזר. רב said 'I do not know' about returning. רבי אלעזר says returning IS protected. They are two different voices.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that extends the protection of a מצוה to the trip home.

phrases.english: It was stated, Rabbi Elazar said:
Those sent on a מצוה are not harmed
neither when going nor when returning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a clear ruling on the question רב could not decide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלוחי מצוה are protected both going and returning.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier תנא רבי אלעזר follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier source רבי אלעזר is based on. It is setting up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the rule. The גמרא wants to find the earlier תנא, the teacher of the ברייתא, who taught this idea.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the basis for רבי אלעזר's rule?

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: animals are protected during עלייה לרגל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר follows איסי בן יהודה. He learns from 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך' that even animals left at home are kept safe while their owners go up to the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא, as it was taught: איסי בן יהודה says: Since the תורה said, 'And no man shall covet your land,' this teaches that your cow will graze in the meadow and no wild animal will harm it, and your chicken will peck in the garbage heap and no weasel will harm it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר follows איסי בן יהודה. He learns from a פסוק about going up to ירושלים that the things people leave behind are protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that no one will take your land while you go up for the רגל. איסי בן יהודה reads this widely: nothing of yours will be harmed, not even unguarded animals that would normally be easy prey.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And no man shall covet your land' (שמות ל״ד:כ״ד)
Weasel or marten, a predator of chickens

phrases.english: Like this tanna, as it was taught:
Isi ben Yehuda says:
Regarding what the Torah said,
"And no man shall covet your land,"
it teaches that your cow will graze in the meadow
and no wild animal will harm it,
your chicken will peck in the garbage heap
and no weasel will harm it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'כמאן' by naming איסי בן יהודה and starting his ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר follows איסי בן יהודה, who learns protection during עלייה לרגל from a פסוק.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from animals to people
steps.stepSummary: If animals that are easily harmed are protected, then people, who are less easily harmed, are surely protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If these animals, which usually get harmed, are not harmed, then people, who usually do not get harmed, all the more so will not be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and uses a קל וחומר to move the protection from animals to the people themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself talks about property left behind. The קל וחומר teaches that the travelers are also protected: if weak, unguarded animals are safe, then people who can defend themselves are surely safe.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: And is this not a kal vachomer?
If these, which usually get harmed,
are not harmed,
people, who usually do not get harmed,
all the more so (they are not harmed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the protection in step 16 from property to people.
steps.raayaObject: People going up for the רגל are themselves protected.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the protected animals in 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך'.

steps.title: Where do we learn protection on the way back?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that so far it has only proven protection on the way there, and asks for a source for the return.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for going. For returning, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap: the proof so far covers only the trip to ירושלים. It sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק for the trip home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the point רב was unsure about. The ברייתא treats returning as something that needs its own source.

phrases.english: I only have it for going;
for returning, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּהֲלִיכָה, בַּחֲזָרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the proof so far covers only going.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for protection on the return trip.

steps.title: 'And you shall go to your tents': safe return home
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ופנית בבקר והלכת לאהליך' teaches that you will return and find your home in peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.' This teaches that you will go and find your tent in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק about going home after the קרבן פסח. It shows that the protection lasts through the return trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'go to your tents' are read as a promise that you will come home safely and find your home whole. This supplies the source for the 'returning' half of רבי אלעזר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents' (דברים ט״ז:ז׳)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's rule (שלוחי מצוה are not harmed, going or returning) is based on איסי בן יהודה. Going comes from 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך' plus a קל וחומר. Returning comes from 'והלכת לאהליך'. רב himself was unsure about returning.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents,"
it teaches that you will go and find
your tent in peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וּפָנִיתָ בַבֹּקֶר וְהָלַכְתָּ לְאֹהָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 and completes the source for רבי אלעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והלכת לאהליך' promises a safe return home, so the return trip is protected too.

steps.title: Why do we need a source for protection on the way there?
steps.stepSummary: Once we know pilgrims are protected even on the way home, why do we need a separate source for the trip there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since they are protected even on the return trip, why do I need a source for the trip there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source from step 16. If we already know the person is protected on the way back, a source for the way there seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the way back, the מצוה is already finished, and still the person is protected. On the way there, he is in the middle of doing the מצוה, so he should surely be protected. That is a simple קל וחומר, so 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך' seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / once it is true that
Why do I need it? (the classic 'this is extra' question)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא doubts that the person is protected on the way there. It agrees he is protected. It only asks why the פסוק is needed to teach it.

phrases.english: And since even on the return trip [he is protected],
phrases.notes: This points back to step 19: 'ופנית בבקר והלכת לאהליך'.

phrases.english: why do I need [a source] for the going?
phrases.notes: The going could be learned by קל וחומר from the return

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּחֲזִירָה, בַּהֲלִיכָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source for the return trip (step 19) to challenge the need for the source for the going (step 16).
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך' to teach protection on the way there
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: protection on the way there follows by קל וחומר from protection on the way back, so the פסוק seems extra.

steps.title: The verse is needed for רבי אמי: only landowners must go up
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is not extra. It teaches רבי אמי's rule that only someone who owns land is obligated to go up to the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רבי אמי's teaching. רבי אמי said: anyone who owns land goes up for the רגל, and anyone who does not own land does not go up for the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק about 'your land' is really needed for a different lesson: רבי אמי's rule about who must go up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ארצך' (your land) shows that the obligation of עליה לרגל applies to someone who owns land. Because the פסוק has this real job, it is no longer 'extra.' Protection on the way there can simply be known through the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: [It is needed] for the teaching of רבי אמי
Goes up [to ירושלים] for the pilgrimage festival

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'ולא יחמד איש את ארצך' is needed for רבי אמי: only a person who owns land has the obligation of עליה לרגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real הלכה about who is obligated in עליה לרגל, learned from a single word ('ארצך').

phrases.english: [It is needed] for the teaching of Rabbi Ami.
For Rabbi Ami said:
Any person who has land —
goes up for the Festival,
and one who does not have land —
does not go up for the Festival.
phrases.notes: We learn this from the word 'ארצך', 'your land'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק was needed only to teach protection on the way there, which is already known by קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches רבי אמי's rule that only landowners must go up. Protection on the way there comes from logic.

steps.title: Why the fruits of גינוסר do not grow in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the special fruits of גינוסר are not found in ירושלים. Otherwise pilgrims would come for the fruit and not for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: Why are there no fruits of גינוסר in ירושלים? So that the pilgrims should not say, 'Even if we came up only to eat the fruits of גינוסר in ירושלים, it would be enough for us.' Then the trip would be made not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we are talking about going up for the רגל, the גמרא brings a related saying. ירושלים was not given the famous fruit of גינוסר, so that people would go up only for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruits of גינוסר were the best around. If they grew in ירושלים, people might travel there for the fruit, and the מצוה would become a side benefit. ה׳ arranged it so the trip stays לשמה, for the sake of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: גינוסר, a fertile area by the כנרת famous for its fruit
Pilgrims going up for the Festivals
It would be enough for us
Not for its own sake (for an outside motive)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין פֵּרוֹת גִּינּוֹסַר בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם?
phrases.english: For what reason are there no fruits of Ginosar in Jerusalem?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: So that the pilgrims should not say:
Had we come up
only to eat the fruits of Ginosar in Jerusalem —
it would be enough for us.
The ascent would turn out to be not for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין פֵּרוֹת גִּינּוֹסַר בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An aggadic side point connected by the shared theme of going up to the רגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גינוסר fruit is kept out of ירושלים so that עליה לרגל stays לשמה.

steps.title: Why the hot springs of טבריא are not in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי gives a parallel idea. The hot springs of טבריא are not in ירושלים, so that pilgrims do not come for the baths.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way, רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי said: Why are the hot springs of טבריא not in ירושלים? So that the pilgrims should not say, 'Even if we came up only to bathe in the hot springs of טבריא, it would be enough for us.' Then the trip would be made not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second example of the same idea. The famous hot springs of טבריא were also kept out of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reasoning as step 22, applied to a pleasure for the body instead of food. Together, the two sayings show a pattern: ירושלים was kept free of 'attractions' so the trip would be for ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to it / in the same way

steps.whatToRemember: Both sayings teach one idea: ירושלים lacks certain delights so that עליה לרגל stays purely for the sake of the מצוה.

phrases.english: Similarly,
Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין חַמֵּי טְבֶרְיָא בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם?
phrases.english: For what reason are the hot springs of Tiberias not in Jerusalem?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: So that the pilgrims should not say:
Had we come up
only to bathe in the hot springs of Tiberias —
it would be enough for us,
and the ascent would turn out to be not for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel example to step 22, with the same structure and reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hot springs of טבריא are kept out of ירושלים so that עליה לרגל stays לשמה.

steps.title: Who mentioned a wine cellar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about searching 'two rows.' It asks why the משנה brings up a cellar when no cellar was mentioned before.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'Regarding what did they say two rows, etc.' Who mentioned a cellar at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and quotes the next line, about searching two rows of barrels in a cellar. It asks why the משנה talks about a cellar as if we already knew about it, and this question sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks 'regarding what did they say two rows in a cellar,' as if an earlier rule about cellars was already stated. But nothing earlier in the משנה mentioned a cellar. So the גמרא wants to know where this background comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding what did they say? (the משנה clarifying an earlier rule)
Two rows (of wine barrels that must be checked)
Who mentioned its name? (it was never brought up)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether a cellar needs to be searched. It is asking a wording question: why does the משנה speak about a cellar as if it was already mentioned?

phrases.english: [The משנה:] 'Regarding what did they say two rows, etc.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה here to start a new topic.

phrases.english: A cellar, who mentioned its name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic side point and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What earlier mention or ruling about a cellar is the משנה building on when it asks 'regarding what did they say two rows'?
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'ובמה אמרו שתי שורות'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה refers back to a cellar ruling that was never stated earlier in the משנה.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: which cellar needs its two rows checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question about the cellar by rereading the משנה. Wine and oil storage rooms need no checking. The 'two rows' rule is for a cellar where חמץ is brought in and wine is fetched during the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: any place where people do not bring חמץ needs no checking. Storage rooms for wine and oil also need no checking. So when did the חכמים say to check two rows in a cellar? They meant a place where people do bring in חמץ, because someone goes in to get more wine during the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. It explains that the משנה's 'two rows in a cellar' refers to a special kind of cellar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the משנה talks about 'a cellar' when it never mentioned one before. The answer is that the משנה has two parts. Ordinary wine storage is exempt, like any room where חמץ is not brought. A cellar that people visit in the middle of the meal to refill wine is different, because they may carry bread in with them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא is rereading a text)
Takes supplies from it, meaning wine fetched during the meal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every wine cellar needs checking. Ordinary wine storage is exempt. Only a cellar people go into during the meal needs its two rows checked.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסִין בּוֹ חָמֵץ —
phrases.english: Any place into which one does not bring chametz
does not require searching,
and wine storages and oil storages
also do not require searching.
And regarding what did they say 'two rows in a cellar'?
A place into which one brings chametz,
phrases.notes: For example, a servant carrying bread goes down to get wine.

phrases.english: and where one takes supplies from it (during the meal).
phrases.notes: The cellar people go into to refill wine mid-meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 about why a cellar suddenly appears in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה (הכי קאמר) into two separate parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'two rows in a cellar' rule seemed to come from nowhere, or to contradict the exemption for wine storage.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain wine storage is exempt. A cellar that wine is fetched from during the meal needs its two rows checked.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the two rows of בית שמאי run from floor to ceiling
steps.stepSummary: Quoting בית שמאי's view in the משנה, רב יהודה explains that the 'two rows' are two full front rows, going from the ground all the way up to the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that בית שמאי require checking two rows, and so on. רב יהודה said: the two rows they meant go from the ground up to the ceiling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי's words from the משנה. רב יהודה then explains what 'two rows' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture barrels stacked in rows on top of each other. According to רב יהודה, you check the front two rows, each one full height from the floor up to the ceiling. These are the barrels a person reaches first when walking in.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceiling ('the heavens of the beam')

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two rows, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: the two rows that they stated
are from the ground up to the ceiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know which cellar is meant, the גמרא defines which rows must be checked according to בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, one checks two full front rows from floor to ceiling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one row shaped like a גאם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. The 'two rows' are really one L-shaped row: the front face from floor to ceiling, plus the top layer going back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is one row shaped like the Greek letter gamma (an L shape).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different explanation of בית שמאי's 'two rows.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, you check the outer front row facing the door, from floor to ceiling. You also check the top row of barrels, running back along the ceiling. Together they form one bent row like the letter Γ, which counts as 'two rows': one standing up and one lying across the top.

keyTerms.meaning: The Greek letter gamma (Γ), an L shape

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה's two rows are both in the front, standing up. רבי יוחנן's 'row' bends: the front face plus the top layer.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
One row, like the shape of a gamma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's definition of the two rows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, one checks the front face and the top layer of barrels, in an L shape.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is a ברייתא supporting each view. It quotes the first one: בית שמאי require two rows across the front of the cellar, from ground to ceiling, just like רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב יהודה, and a ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן. The one that agrees with רב יהודה: בית שמאי say two rows across the whole front of the cellar, and the two rows they meant go from the ground up to the ceiling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first announces that each אמורא has a supporting ברייתא. Then it brings the ברייתא that matches רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses almost the same words as רב יהודה: 'from the ground up to the ceiling.' This shows that רב יהודה's reading has an older source behind it. It does not end the debate, because רבי יוחנן also has a ברייתא, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda,
and a baraita was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan.
It was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת עַל פְּנֵי כׇּל הַמַּרְתֵּף,
phrases.english: two rows across the entire front of the cellar,
and the two rows that they stated
are from the ground up to the ceiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source supporting the view of step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that the two rows go from floor to ceiling
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting בית שמאי with the same wording

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא describes the outer row facing the door and the top row facing the ceiling. The rows further in and the rows lower down need no checking. This matches רבי יוחנן's L shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבי יוחנן: two rows across the whole cellar. The outer row is the one that faces the door, and the upper row is the one that faces the ceiling. The rows further inside than the outer one, and the rows below the top one, do not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא names one row facing the door and one row facing the ceiling. That is exactly the front face plus the top layer, the 'gamma' shape. The גמרא leaves both views standing, each with its own support.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's 'two rows': for רב יהודה, two front rows from floor to ceiling. For רבי יוחנן, the front face plus the top layer (an L shape). Each view has a supporting ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת עַל פְּנֵי כׇּל הַמַּרְתֵּף —
phrases.english: two rows across the entire cellar:
the outer one, which faces the doorway,
and the upper one, which faces the ceiling beam.
The rows inward from it and the rows below it
do not require searching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the matching support for the other side, step 27.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא naming the row facing the door and the row facing the ceiling

steps.title: בית הלל's two rows, and רב's explanation
steps.stepSummary: Quoting בית הלל's view in the משנה, רב explains that the two rows are the top row of barrels on the front face and the row right below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that בית הלל require only the two outer rows, which are the upper ones. רב said: this means the top one and the one below it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to בית הלל's easier view in the משנה. רב explains which two rows they meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל require less checking than בית שמאי. For רב, you check only the front face, and only its top two rows: the uppermost row and the row under it. Both of these face outward toward the door.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, who are more lenient here

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
the two outer rows, which are the upper ones.
Rav said:
the uppermost one and the one below it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת הַחִיצוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵן הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת. אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית שמאי's view to בית הלל's view in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, one checks the top row of the front face and the row just below it.

steps.title: שמואל: the top front row and the row behind it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. The two rows are the top front row and the top row just inward from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the top one and the one further inside from it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different explanation of בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, both rows are on the top layer: the front top row and the row behind it. For רב, both rows are on the front face: the top row and the row beneath it. Each one takes a different word in the משנה as the main guide.

keyTerms.meaning: The one further inside from it

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
the uppermost one and the one inward from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, one checks the top front row and the top row just behind it.

steps.title: Asking for רב's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what led רב to his explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב read בית הלל the way he did. This sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about רב's source in the words of the משנה. It is not an attack. It is a request to see how he reads the text.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of רב's view from step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in the משנה led רב to his explanation

steps.title: רב focuses on the word 'outer'
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the word 'outer' closely. Both rows must face outward, so both are on the front face.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reads the word 'outer' precisely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב built his view on the word 'outer.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both rows are 'outer,' both must face the door. The top front row and the row under it both face out. The top row behind the front one, which שמואל includes, does not face out.

phrases.english: He reads precisely: 'outer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב reads the word 'outer' to mean that both rows face the doorway.

steps.title: But the משנה also says 'upper'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the משנה also calls the rows 'upper,' which sounds like both should be on top, as שמואל says.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה also says 'upper'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with the other word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'outer' means both rows face out, then 'upper' should mean both rows are on top. רב's lower barrel is not on top. So the word 'upper' seems to support שמואל instead.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (a challenge from the text)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'upper'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 33.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'upper' seems to require both rows to be on top, which fits שמואל and not רב.

steps.title: 'Upper' only rules out the lowest barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רב. The word 'upper' does not mean 'on the very top layer.' It comes to exclude the lower barrels of the front face.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the lowest of the low ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by explaining what the word 'upper' comes to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'outer' tells us both rows are on the front face. 'Upper' tells us to check only the top part of that face, not the rows near the floor. So both words fit his view, and his two rows are the top two rows of the front face.

keyTerms.meaning: The lowest of the lower ones (the bottom barrels)

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's two rows: for רב, the top front row and the row below it ('outer' is the main word). For שמואל, the top front row and the top row behind it. For רב, 'upper' only rules out the lower front rows.

phrases.english: To exclude the lowest of the lower ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word 'upper' as a word that excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Upper' means both rows must be on the top layer.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Upper' only excludes the lower front barrels. Both rows are the top two on the front face.

steps.title: What is the source for שמואל's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates שמואל's position (top row and the row behind it) and asks what led him to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the top row and the row just inward from it. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates שמואל's view and asks what in the משנה led him to it. This sets up the next step, which gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question the גמרא asked about רב in Step 32, now asked about שמואל. שמואל's two rows are both on the top layer, one behind the other, going into the cellar. The גמרא wants to know which word in the משנה points to that picture.

keyTerms.meaning: The one further inside from it

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This repeats שמואל's view from step 31, so the question can build on it.

phrases.english: The uppermost row and the one inward from it.
phrases.notes: Both rows are on the top layer, one behind the other.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The question that opens the explanation of שמואל's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רב (Steps 32-35), the גמרא turns to explaining שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in the משנה is the basis of שמואל's explanation?

steps.title: שמואל reads the word 'upper' closely
steps.stepSummary: שמואל relies on the word 'upper' (עליונות), so both rows must be on the top layer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reads the word 'upper rows' closely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל builds his view on the word עליונות ('upper rows') in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says the rows are 'upper', שמואל reasons that both rows must be on the top layer. So he places them one behind the other on top, not one above the other on the front face. This mirrors how רב relied on the word 'outer' in Step 33.

keyTerms.meaning: He reads precisely / infers from the wording
Upper (rows), a word in the משנה

phrases.english: He infers from the word 'upper rows'.
phrases.notes: Both rows must be upper, meaning on the top layer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'upper' teaches that both rows are on the top layer.

steps.title: But the משנה also says 'outer'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the משנה also uses the word 'outer', which seems to support רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה also teaches 'outer'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with the other word in the משנה, 'outer' (חיצונה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב used the word 'outer' to show that both rows face outward on the front of the cellar. If the משנה says 'outer', how can שמואל place the second row inside, behind the front row? This is the mirror image of the challenge to רב in Step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: Outer (row), a word in the משנה
But it teaches! (introduces a challenge from a text)

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'outer'?
phrases.notes: The word רב relied on now challenges שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in Step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the second row is inward, behind the front row
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Outer' implies both rows face the outside, which fits רב and not שמואל.

steps.title: 'Outer' only excludes the deep inner rows
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, the word 'outer' comes to exclude the rows deep inside the cellar, not to require both rows on the front face.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the innermost of the inner rows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל: the word 'outer' is meant only to rule out the barrels deep inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Outer' does not mean 'on the front face only.' It means 'not the far inside rows.' The top front row and the one just behind it still count as outer compared to everything deeper in the cellar. This matches how רב explained away 'upper' in Step 35.

phrases.english: To exclude the innermost of the inner rows.
phrases.notes: Only the two outermost rows need checking; deeper rows do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה as an exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Outer' means both rows must be on the front face.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Outer' only excludes the deep inner rows, so a second top row just behind the front one is still fine.

steps.title: Which תנאים support each view
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches a ברייתא like רב, but all the other תנאים teach like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא teaches like רב, and all the תנאים teach like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports which sources back each side: רבי חייא's version supports רב, and all the other reciters of ברייתות support שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'תנאים' means the people who memorized and recited the ברייתות in the study hall. Each side has a source, but שמואל has the clear majority. This sets up the ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (a ברייתא) in line with his view
Here: the reciters who memorized ברייתות

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תנאים' does not mean the sages of the משנה era. It means the reciters in the בית מדרש who memorized ברייתות by heart.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya teaches in accordance with Rav,
phrases.notes: His version of the ברייתא supports רב.

phrases.english: and all the reciters
phrases.notes: All the other reciters of ברייתות.

phrases.english: teach in accordance with Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The majority supports שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views have been defended, the גמרא turns to outside sources.
steps.raayaObject: The views of רב and שמואל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתות: רבי חייא's version supports רב; all the other reciters support שמואל

steps.title: The הלכה follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like שמואל: check the top front row and the row just behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we follow שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling fits the majority of ברייתות reported in Step 40. In practice, in a wine cellar you check the top row of barrels at the front and the top row just behind it. You do not have to check the lower barrels on the front face.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: two rows on the front face (relies on 'outer'). שמואל: the top front row plus the top row behind it (relies on 'upper'). Each explains away the other's word. The הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical scope of בדיקת חמץ in a storage area full of barrels.

phrases.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Shmuel.
phrases.notes: The final practical ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules based on the support reported in Step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One checks the top front row of barrels and the top row just inward from it, following שמואל.
